newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Army general put at head of shaky Zaire government.
newsitem.headline: Army general put at head of shaky Zaire government.

text.p: Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko put a loyal army general in charge of his shaky government on Wednesday as turmoil unleashed by a rebel war gripped the capital.
Mobutu named General Likulia Bolongo, a military judge who is defence minister in an outgoing cabinet, to replace Prime Minister Etienne Tshisekedi, effectively sacked.
Likulia was a key link man between Mobutu and opposition politicians pressing for multi-party rule at the height of the pro-democracy campaign between 1990 and 1992.
Political analysts said it is a role he could well play again if Mobutu yields to pressure from opponents and even foreign allies to negotiate an end to his 32-year rule.
The United States signalled on Wednesday that Mobutu should step down, effectively ending a decades-old alliance with the African strongman.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said a negotiated solution to Zaire's civil war, which Washington has been pressing for, must include agreements on interim transitional government arrangements leading ultimately to elections.
Tshisekedi's teeming army of fanatical township followers clashed with security forces in the capital on Tuesday and Wednesday as it became clear Tshisekedi was about to be dropped.

Mobutu used emergency powers he decreed on Tuesday to appoint Likulia, an intellectually inclined officer who attended colleges in France and was once a university administrator in Zaire. He is well known in international military legal circles.

His appointment came on a day of worsening street clashes in Kinshasa during which Mobutu's own army officer son Kongolo, whose nickname is Saddam Hussein, headed the crackdown on pro-Tshisekedi militants.

Neither Likulia's appointment nor the use of troops in Kinshasa appeared to cow the militants, who overwhelmingly back rebel leader Laurent Kabila's bid to topple Mobutu. Kabila's rebels entered the second city of Lubumbashi on Wednesday.
"We won't take this lying down. They will find us in their path," a Tshisekedi supporter said on hearing of the change of prime minister.
Born on July 8, 1938, Likulia joined the then colonial army in 1958 and became an artillery officer before switching to military justice.
He obtained a doctorate degree from the University of Aix-en-Provence, France, in 1970.
On his return home he was appointed alternate judge of the Zaire Armed Forces with the rank of lieutenant-colonel. He became the army's chief judge a year later with the full rank of colonel.
He was promoted to the rank of general and given command of a division in 1977 before becoming secretary of state at the defence ministry from 1985 to 1990.
Likulia is a member of Zaire's permanent commission on law reform and a board member of the international society of military penal code and laws governing warfare.
He has been decorated at home as well as in France and Belgium.
Likulia was appointed defence minister last December in a war cabinet formed by then prime minister Kengo wa Dondo, voted out of power by parliament about three weeks ago.
